text:
Maria Gutierrez: Quick sync — we need to pick a strategy for transient ingest load spikes (Kinesis throttles). Do we prioritize tail latency and shed/route, or preserve durability with buffering to S3 (higher cost + slower recovery)? Need a short-term plan for the next sprint.
Devin Cho: what's our customer-facing SLA for ingestion? internal SLAs?
Maria Gutierrez: customer-facing is 99.9% successful ingestion within 30s for Hosted tier. Dedicated can be softer. Internal ops want no silent loss.
Kai Patel: my +1 is a hybrid: local ephemeral raft of small buffers (memstore per shard) for quick retries + overflow to S3 when memstore > X. That keeps most traffic low-latency, but still guarantees eventual durability. Ops cost is running per-node disk/cache and extra state machine complexity.
Andrea Lopez: +1 hybrid but worried about cost and egress. We should quantify S3 PUT + GET + lifecycle. Also need to avoid doubling writes for normal traffic.
Sam Nguyen: If we add a memstore we can tune thresholds to avoid the S3 path 99% of the time. I'll run a sim with current traffic percentiles and burst distributions.
Devin Cho: alternative is backpressure to callers (HTTP 429) with short retry hints. Simpler but breaks PLG UX and pushes complexity to clients.
Kai Patel: 429s acceptable for internal infra but not for end-user endpoints. We might combine: low-priority requests get 429, high-priority (SLA) get the buff->S3 fallback. Need a route-key in envelope.
Maria Gutierrez: agree on route-key. We already have billing_key and priority in envelope. Let's reuse 'ingest_priority' field. Document the semantics: high=guaranteed durability, low=best-effort/429.
ingest-bot: deploy of ingest-proxy v2 scheduled to canary at 2026-04-02T09:00Z — will include header passthrough for ingest_priority.
Andrea Lopez: operational checklist: 1) define memstore size per shard, 2) S3 object layout + TTL/compaction job, 3) metrics to surface S3 fallback rate and cost, 4) rollout plan (canary + traffic split).
Devin Cho: metrics we need: fallback.rate, fallback.bytes, avg-fallback-latency, memstore.fill_pct, 429.rate by route. Also alert when fallback.rate > 0.5% of requests for >1h.
Sam Nguyen: I'll prototype memstore + overflow logic in the test harness. Quick config suggestion: 
```
memstore.capacity_mb: 128
memstore.spill_threshold_pct: 85
spill.target_s3_prefix: s3://redwood-ingest-overspill/{env}/{shard}/
spill.batch_size: 512
spill.max_retries: 5
```
Kai Patel: looks reasonable. consider async compaction job to combine small objects into daily segments to reduce S3 request cost. Also set lifecycle 7d->glacier for cold data.
Andrea Lopez: raise a concern: how do we attribute cost to customers? If we write overflow to S3 for a customer, we need per-tenant accounting. Batching across tenants makes attribution harder.
Maria Gutierrez: policy: we should try to keep per-tenant isolation for billing. If spill includes mixed tenants, we must record per-object metadata mapping batches to tenants. Could be a header in the object or sidecar index.
Devin Cho: sidecar index (small DynamoDB) per spill file with tenant-chunk offsets seems simplest for queries/cost attribution. Query path for cost jobs reads index and sums bytes. Tradeoff: extra DB ops and consistency.
Sam Nguyen: I'll include tenant offsets in the spill manifest. Simpler prototype first: write per-tenant spill files (easier attribution but more objects). We'll measure cost impact.
Kai Patel: ops note: many small objects -> S3 request cost. If per-tenant spills create explosion, fallback to manifest approach. Good to measure with traffic replay.
Andrea Lopez: Decision checklist for RFC: technical approach (memstore+S3 overflow), envelope change (ingest_priority), metrics/alerts list, billing attribution approach (per-tenant file OR manifest), compaction/lifecycle policy, rollout steps.
Maria Gutierrez: Action items: Andrea to draft RFC doc with checklist and SLO mapping (due EOD Friday). Sam to run cost sims + replay (ETA Tue). Devin to propose alert thresholds and dashboard widgets (ETA Mon). Kai to prototype compaction approach and estimate added ops complexity (ETA Wed).
Sam Nguyen: noted. I'll post the simulation results in this thread when ready.
Devin Cho: +1 on timeline. If we hit higher-than-expected S3 exposure we can gate SLOs for public beta.
Maria Gutierrez: thanks team. tagging @Andrea @Sam @Devin @Kai — let's reconvene after the RFC draft. :thumbsup:
